families.name: Sales & Revenue Operations
families.what: The team behind the sales team. You keep the CRM clean, build reports and dashboards on the pipeline, set up territories and quotas, and fix the processes that slow sellers down. You support sales without carrying a quota.
families.why: Uses Excel, CRM tools, and reporting from an IS degree plus an understanding of how selling works. Sales experience is a real advantage here.

families.name: Business Systems & CRM Admin
families.what: You run the software a company uses every day (Salesforce, HubSpot, an ERP like SAP, an HR system like Workday). You gather what people need, change settings, build fields and reports, test updates, and train users. Mostly configuration, not coding.
families.why: This is what Systems Analysis and Design and Information Systems Management courses are built for.

families.name: Implementation & Onboarding
families.what: When a company buys software, you get them set up: learn what they need, configure the product, move their data over, and train their team. Project work with customers, usually with heavy training at the start.
families.why: Mixes technical setup with talking to customers, so it rewards both an IS background and sales or service experience.

families.name: Customer Success & Tech Support
families.what: You keep customers happy after the sale: answer questions, solve problems, run check ins, and help them get value from the product so they renew. Support roles troubleshoot issues and escalate the hard ones.
families.why: Customer facing work where explaining technical things clearly matters more than coding.

families.name: Business & Operations Analyst
families.what: You turn data into decisions: pull numbers, build reports and dashboards, spot problems, and recommend fixes for operations, supply chain, marketing, or the business overall.
families.why: Excel, Tableau, data mining, and operations coursework line up directly.

families.name: Rotational & Trainee Programs
families.what: Structured new grad programs that rotate you through departments and train you for management or a specialty. Built for people with little experience.
families.why: Designed for graduating seniors. Your degree and any work experience count.
